tier_reason: Issue #2196 runs the public HarfBuzz harness perf/benchmark-font.cc (same hb_font calls for both backends via hb_font_set_funcs_using, 'fontations' vs 'ot') at HarfBuzz commit eff2d6b9 and Fontations commit ec902bd2, with the HarfBuzz build stated (Clang 21.1.7, meson --buildtype=release (-O3) -Db_lto=true), the Rust build stated (1.94.0-nightly 2025-12-20, fat LTO, one codegen unit), the command line, and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, pinned to CPU 6, seven repetitions, CPU medians): code, compiler, flags and CPU model are all present, so A stands for a mostly-slower result.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed and mostly slower; Fontations is not faster than HarfBuzz OT overall. Issue #2196 geometric means of Fontations/OT time over 12 fixture/instance cases (above 1 means Fontations is slower): nominal glyphs 1.53x, horizontal advances 1.39x, vertical origins 1.58x, glyph extents 1.29x, drawing 1.51x, load face and shape 1.05x; from the page's CPU-median list, paint is about 1.26x slower in every case and vertical advances 1.03-1.16x slower (geometric mean 1.11x) (derived from page data). Faster rows: varied Roboto Flex (wght=500) vertical origins 1,590 us (OT) vs 1,020 us (Fontations), 0.64x; varied Roboto Flex glyph extents 1,540 us vs 966 us, 0.63x; Adobe VF Prototype CFF2 glyph extents 0.87x (default) and 0.89x (wght=500); nominal glyphs 0.99x on Roboto-Regular and Source Sans Pro and about 0.97x on Source Serif Variable (derived from page data); Noto Nastaliq Urdu load face and shape 2,089 us (OT) vs 2,055 us (Fontations), about 0.98x (derived from page data). Worst rows: Noto Serif Myanmar nominal glyphs 3.12x slower, varied Adobe CFF2 vertical origins 2.86x and horizontal advances 2.74x slower. No FreeType library timing is on the page (the 'FreeType' rows in the supplied-gvar-scalars table are a skrifa drawing style).
corrections.caveats: Weak 'faster' evidence: issue #2196 is a performance-gap report by the HarfBuzz maintainer (behdad; page shows opened 4 October 2026, updated 3 October 2026, still open). Fontations is slower than HarfBuzz OT in most rows (unvaried glyf extents and origins about 1.7-1.8x slower, unhinted drawing about 1.5x slower, paint about 1.26x slower, varied Adobe CFF2 advances 2.74x slower) and faster in a handful of varied-instance cases. The Fontations side measured commit ec902bd2, which is a head commit of the open, unmerged PR #2197 ('Reduce font model variation and lookup overhead', not on main), built with local Cargo patches for read-fonts 0.45.0, skrifa 0.48.0 and font-types 0.12.6; the HarfBuzz side was tuned in the same effort (HarfBuzz PR #6318, commit 5d86ce2980), so the table is a snapshot of in-flight optimisation on both sides and released crates may differ. Fontations is timed through HarfBuzz's font-funcs FFI layer (hb_font_set_funcs_using 'fontations'), so the numbers include that glue rather than standalone skrifa calls. They cover the font model only, not shaping or rasterization; there is no direct skrifa versus FreeType timing (the README's Performance section only points to HarfBuzz perf/README.md; fauntlet compares output, not speed). Some tables in the issue (supplied gvar scalars, PR #2197 numbers) used Rust 1.89 rather than the 1.94 nightly of the main table.

notes: All claimed numbers match the issue page and the harness does identical work for both backends, so the record is confirmed at A as a flagged mostly-slower entry (keep-and-document). HarfBuzz build is stated (Clang 21.1.7, release -O3, LTO); the measured Fontations code is an unmerged PR branch, which belongs in the shortcoming.

tier_reason: The README claims 'way smaller and much faster' than ICU, GNU libunistring and libutf8proc with no numbers, and no result, hardware or flags file exists in the repo; benchmark/character.c and benchmark/utf8-decode.c compare against libutf8proc only and print ratios at run time, never published. A 'twice as fast as libutf8proc' remark exists only in a search snippet of a blocked May 2022 suckless dev mailing-list post (no methodology, pre-3.0 code), which is not enough to lift the tier here.

corrections.baseline: libutf8proc (the only library the repo's benchmark/ programs compare against: grapheme cluster break and UTF-8 decode); the README also names ICU and GNU libunistring, but no benchmark against them exists
corrections.workload: Repo benchmark/: character.c times grapheme_is_character_break against utf8proc_grapheme_break_stateful over the Unicode grapheme-break conformance test codepoints (100,000 iterations); utf8-decode.c times grapheme_decode_utf8 against utf8proc_iterate over the same strings encoded as UTF-8. word.c, sentence.c, line.c and case.c time libgrapheme alone (no comparison), and bidirectional.c is an empty stub. Timing uses clock() (CPU time) in benchmark/util.c, which prints the percentage faster or slower than the first run.
corrections.caveats: Tier D slot: the claim is qualitative. The repo ships benchmark programs (make benchmark, links -lutf8proc) but publishes no results, hardware or flags; no ICU or libunistring benchmark exists. Benchmark asymmetries a reproducer should know: libgrapheme is linked statically (libgrapheme.a) while libutf8proc is linked dynamically; the wrapper functions are marked optnone under clang; the default config.mk builds with -Os; and the UTF-8 decode run itself labels libutf8proc 'unsafe (does not detect overlong encodings)', so the two decoders do different validation work. A search snippet of a blocked May 2022 suckless dev mailing-list post by the author says libgrapheme became 'twice as fast' as libutf8proc for grapheme cluster counting (snippet only, no methodology, code predating the 3.0.0 LUT rework). README conformance section still says Unicode 15.0.0 while the intro says 17.0.0 (version 3.0.0, 2025-12-24). The library is a grapheme, word, sentence and line-break segmenter plus case converter, not a shaper, so it belongs in unicode-utf8. Canonical repo is git.suckless.org/libgrapheme (blocked here); the GitHub copy has 15 stars.

notes: No number exists in the repo; confirmed at D. Category should move from font-shaping-text-layout to unicode-utf8 (category is not a correctable field here, so set it through decisions.json). License ISC, last commit 2025-12-24 and 15 stars confirmed.
